about: Known, unreported or unfixed PostgreSQL bugs the fuzz runner can hit: the one list build-patched.sh and pretriage.py read. Paths are relative to the case-studies directory (the parent of postgresql-coverage). fix: how to build PostgreSQL master with the bug fixed. kind core (a full build of the patched tree) or contrib (only contrib/<dir> rebuilt via PGXS against a copy of the master install); sources: the patch, first available wins: {path, strip} a file applied as `patch -p<strip> -d <tree>`, or {git: {base, head}} the diff of two commits of the PostgreSQL clone; obtain: how to get a source that is not saved locally; optional: built only with build-patched.sh --with-optional (the patch is not saved in this repository). signatures: how the bug shows in a run (sqlstate, errors: regular expressions over the finding's message, runner_signatures: regular expressions over the signature directory, finding_kinds: failure, crash, memory, hangs, timeouts). reproduce: single-session (a finding's replay shows it) or needs-concurrency (a single-session replay cannot: such a finding is not-reproduced, and says so). check: SQL run by `psql -X -q -At -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -v VERBOSITY=sqlstate -f -` (stdout and stderr together) in a fresh database of a throwaway cluster, PATH, PGHOST, PGPORT and PGUSER set for \! lines; expected: its exact output on a fixed build; limits: seconds and rss_mb the check must stay within as well (a backend over rss_mb is killed). excluded_by: what keeps the generator or the runner from reporting it. status: open, or fixed once master has the fix (then fixed_in records it and the entry stays as the record).

bugs.summary: Planner use-after-free: add_partial_path() frees a partial Path that a Gather built in apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths() still points to (the Path is shared by the scan/join rel and final_rel); create_plan then reads freed memory: ERROR XX000 unrecognized node type: <n> (n varies by build). Reachable since 8300d3ad4aa.

bugs.excluded_by: ephyra-postgresql src/sqlancer.rs known_error ("unrecognized node type:"): the oracles skip it (known_skips) and the runner counts it as known, not a finding (since 3ce90ab). A finding with it means a runner binary older than that, or a path where the oracle does not apply known_error (a case statement: model-statement-*-XX000).

bugs.summary: VACUUM FULL / CLUSTER / CREATE INDEX fail with "missing chunk number 0 for toast value N in pg_toast_M" (XX001): a RECENTLY_DEAD heap tuple whose TOAST chunks on-access pruning already removed under a newer horizon (cached by a lazy VACUUM of an unrelated table), while a transaction in another database holds an older XID. Class of BUG #18351 / #19519.

bugs.summary: btree_gist date_ops: gbt_date_penalty (and the KNN distances, and date <-> date) call date_mi, which refuses infinite dates: inserting 'infinity' into a GiST index on a date of more than one page, inserting any date into one that holds an infinity, or a KNN scan over one fails with "cannot subtract infinite dates" (22008).
bugs.excluded_by: ephyra-postgresql src/semantics.rs gist_dates_ok (cac530c): a GiST index is keyed on a date column only if the column never held an infinite date, and such a column is never written one; the oracles also skip 22008 as a plan-dependent error (sqlancer::expected_error), so only a case statement (model-statement-*-22008) can show it
bugs.expected_from: pretriage.py --expected on master 158b6d5109 with fix.patch (contrib build via PGXS), 2026-10-14; master prints `ERROR:  22008` after q1 (twice, and 500|0), after q2 (twice) and after q3

bugs.summary: Nested BETWEEN grows exponentially in parse analysis (transformAExprBetween copies its operand), and transformExprRecurse never checks for interrupts, so statement_timeout and pg_cancel_backend wait for it: a backend allocating >1 GB/s past its timeout, until a memory kill.

sources.note: our CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() in transformExprRecurse: makes it cancellable, does not remove the blowup

bugs.reproduce_note: shows as a resource finding (a memory kill, a hang, or a signal-9 crash when the OS killed the backend), not a wrong result or an error; pretriage replays such findings with a short statement_timeout (--resource-timeout) under the memory and time watchdog: master runs past it until killed, the patched build cancels
bugs.expected_from: the output is the same on master (once parse analysis ends); the limits tell them apart: master's backend passes 1.6 GB (killed at 600 MB), the patched build cancels at about 0.1 s and 160 MB (report.md)
bugs.excluded_by: ephyra-postgresql src/expr.rs MAX_DEPTH = 8 (expression nesting; at most 2^8 copies), and the runner's --max-rss-mb memory kill and statement timeout bound what a run spends on one

bugs.summary: Since 8f29467c57f (19 BETA1..RC1, master) BuildTupleHashTable no longer caps its initial size at hash_mem, and RecursiveUnion and hashed SetOp pass the planner's raw group estimate: ExecInit allocates and zeroes up to 2^32 x 16 B = 64 GiB before reading a row. A recursive UNION (default settings) or a hashed EXCEPT/INTERSECT (when the sorted path is disabled too) fails with 53200 out of memory, or the backend grows until a memory kill.

sources.note: our patch (report.md): the hash_mem cap restored in BuildTupleHashTable

bugs.reproduce_note: an oracle variant that disables a plan type (plans-*, generic) often picks the oversized hashed node, so it shows as 'the original succeeds, the variant fails' as well as 53200 and memory kills; those signatures are too generic to match on, so the patched build's replay decides
bugs.expected_from: by hand from report.md (the patched build returns 1000000 at 113 MB peak, no rows, 0); master passes 1 GB on q1 (killed at 600 MB) and allocates 32/64 GiB on q2/q3. Confirm with pretriage.py --expected hashsetop-out-of-memory.
bugs.excluded_by: none: the generator writes recursive CTEs and set operations, and the plans oracle's variants disable sort/hash plan types; the runner's --max-rss-mb memory kill bounds a run's cost

bugs.summary: CLUSTER (index-scan path) and REPACK drop a live row that the transaction inserted and then updated in a rolled-back subtransaction: HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuumHorizon returns INSERT_IN_PROGRESS without setting HEAP_XMAX_INVALID, rewrite_heap_tuple parks the row waiting for its aborted successor, and rewrite_heap_dead_tuple frees it. Silent loss of committed data, all supported branches.

bugs.summary: The parallel executor's DSM and instrumentation walks (execParallel.c) visit a SubPlan's one PlanState once per Parallel Append child that references it, so its nodes are set up twice. Since a241bc4fede (master, 2026-10-12, Material storage instrumentation) EXPLAIN ANALYZE with default settings crashes assert builds: TRAP Assert("toc->toc_entry[i].key != key") in shm_toc_insert; Sort, IncrementalSort, Hash, Agg, Memoize and SeqScan IO instrumentation crash 19rc1 assert builds the same way (the assert is 43222b8e53f, master/19); without asserts and on 14-18, EXPLAIN ANALYZE counts the SubPlan's nodes 4x and loses per-worker details.
bugs.upstream: BUG #19766 (pgsql-bugs, 2026-10-16, short report without a fix): https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/19766-c3d105a4e0ec5487@postgresql.org

sources.note: ours (report.md): the four walkers skip a plan node already visited; regression test in partition_prune

bugs.expected_from: by hand: the patched build runs the EXPLAIN (output discarded, workers launched vary); master crashes the backend there. Confirm with pretriage.py --expected parallel-material-dup-toc.
bugs.excluded_by: none: the views oracle runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE of every query, and the generator writes partitioned tables and IN (subquery)

bugs.summary: A bug in the v7 TOAST patch (cfbot cf/6824) of toast-missing-chunk-vacuum-full, not in master: when VACUUM FULL / CLUSTER (no sort) scans an UPDATE's old version before its live successor and the old version's TOAST is gone, rewrite_heap_tuple() writes the successor, then fails on the parked old version and returns false for the caller's live tuple: TRAP Assert("recently_dead") in heapam_relation_copy_for_cluster (heapam_handler.c:993). Without asserts the outcome is correct.
